name: fast_keywords
hypothesis: matchesKeyword compiles a fresh regex per keyword per call; planPrompt triggers >1000 probes per prompt, so regex construction dominates the hot path. Precompiling one matcher per unique keyword and memoizing lowercased text should cut p95 by >=15% with zero accuracy regression.
mechanism: Two bounded caches: (1) KEYWORD_CACHE Map<keyword, {lower,isPhrase,wordRegex}> precomputes the classifier + word-boundary RegExp once per keyword string; phrase keywords avoid regex entirely (substring includes). (2) TEXT_LOWER_CACHE Map<text, lower> memoizes text.toLowerCase() so the same prompt passed through hundreds of hasAny/keywordScore calls lowercases once (LRU-bounded at 512). hasAny/countMatches were rewritten as direct loops instead of reduce/some to skip the per-iter matchesKeyword call overhead. Semantics preserved exactly: single-word keywords still use \b-bounded regex, multi/punctuated keywords still use substring, both case-insensitive. Edge cases (regex metachars, empty strings, case folding) are unchanged because they flow through the same escapeRegex + toLowerCase path, just cached.

baselineRemeasured.note: Re-run on same machine in same session to eliminate hardware/load variance vs frontier.json.

testSummary.note: 4 failures are pre-existing (validate-context-bench + prompt-planner corpus tests); identical to baseline.
